topic: Are existing link budget margins sufficient to handle SINR degradation from accumulated inter-beam interference in full frequency reuse scenarios?
consensus_response: In full frequency reuse (FFR) scenarios, the accumulation of inter-beam interference (IBI) leads to a significant reduction in signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), moving the link from a power-limited to an interference-limited regime. This degradation is exacerbated by intra-system interferences reducing useful signal power at receivers, resulting in higher utilization of lower modulation and coding schemes (modcods) and increased outage probability. The multiuser satellite environment further exacerbates this issue, requiring innovative solutions to mitigate IBI's impact on system performance. As a result, existing link budget margins are insufficient to handle SINR degradation from accumulated inter-beam interference in FFR scenarios.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of full frequency reuse (FFR) in satellite communication systems, including the reduction in signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) due to inter-beam interference (IBI). Studies have shown that IBI leads to a higher utilization of lower modcods and increased outage probability, burdening the system in terms of efficiency. The multiuser satellite environment exacerbates this issue, requiring innovative solutions to ensure reliable communication services.
